judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence carving intrafamily automobile liability out of the cross-suits exclusion; narrow and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes personal auto/intrafamily exposure that a corporate hospital policy does not have, a mild misfit with the Named Insured definition (c020) but not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical execution-clause substitution; nothing to construe, though it recites the form as 'UML-002 (4/91)' where the attached form is dated 1/91.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The date mismatch with the actual policy jacket is a small cross-reference error but has no coverage consequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence merges two alternative methods (surrender, or mailing notice) without a conjunction, so when cancellation by the insured takes effect is not cleanly stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It restates Condition 12 (c055) without saying it replaces it, and Item 6 of the Declarations imposes a short-rate minimum premium on insured cancellation that this clause ignores.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare lead-in line with no operative content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It introduces subparagraphs (a)-(e) which themselves conflict with Condition 12 (c055) and Endorsement No. 3 (c092), but the lead-in adds nothing of its own.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific and numerically precise (less than 60 days in force, 10 days' notice).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its ten-day notice cannot stand with Endorsement No. 3 (c092), which requires sixty days' written notice of any cancellation, nor with Condition 12's thirty days (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Concrete non-payment cancellation right with a stated ten-day notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Same conflict: Endorsement No. 3 (c092) promises sixty days' notice 'in the event of cancellation', and the Pay Plan endorsement (c098) defines when payments are past due.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exhaustive list of three grounds with a reasonableness qualifier on 'substantial change in the risk'; 'substantial' is soft but the list is closed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The ten-day notice again collides with the sixty days promised in Endorsement No. 3 (c092) and the thirty days in Condition 12 (c055).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is conditioned on a policy term longer than one year and its opening words ('if in addition to the right ... and provided that if') are grammatically broken.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declared policy period is a single year (Item 2), so the provision has no application here; that is inoperativeness rather than conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A right to renewal 'on the terms then being applied by the Company to similar risks' is vague as to price and terms, and 'a right te to renewal' is a mechanical slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its sixty-day non-renewal notice matches Endorsement No. 3 (c092) but sits oddly with the shorter cancellation notices in (a)-(c) and with Item 6's short-rate provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second sentence — 'Any person or organization or the legal representative thereof shall be entitled to recover under this policy to the extent of the insurance afforded' — drops the usual judgment/agreement precondition and so reads far more broadly than intended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly deletes and replaces Condition 6 (c049), whose no-joinder sentence still appears in the policy text, and it interacts with the no-action condition precedent of full compliance against the Wisconsin conditions in c072-c073.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence stating a make-whole rule; the phrase 'fully compensated for damages' is undefined but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reverses the priority order set out in the subrogation waterfall (c053), which reimburses interests paying above the retained limit and then the company, so the two must be harmonised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory imputation-of-knowledge rule, precisely worded, though it cites 'WI Statutes Section 637.09' where the intended reference appears to be 631.09.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It flatly contradicts Condition 11 (c054), which says notice to or knowledge of any agent effects no waiver and does not estop the company.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Tracks the statute closely with clear materiality and contribution-to-loss tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts back the preamble's reliance on declarations statements (c001) and the Condition 13 warranty of maintenance of underlying insurance (c056), a qualification rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any insured subject of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act' is ungrammatical and the exclusion's reach — fiduciary duties only, or any pension-related liability — is not clear from the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No other provision addresses employee benefit plan liability; the D&O exclusion (c076-c078) covers adjacent but distinct ground.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three broad limbs, the last extending to property 'as to which any insured, his agents or subcontractors are for any purpose exercising physical control', which is very wide but expressly so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It states a materially different care-custody-control rule from the policy's own exclusion (c024), which is limited to property the insured is contractually obliged to insure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'directors and officers are excluded from this contract for liability arising out of wrongful acts' is loosely drafted — it excludes persons rather than coverage — but 'wrongful acts' is defined next.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out in c078 restores cover for personal injury, bodily injury, property damage and hospital professional liability, which is nearly everything this umbrella insures, and it conflicts with the insured definition (c021) naming executive officers and directors as insureds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional wrongful-acts definition, though the closing reference to 'the company' is ambiguous as between the insurer and the insured entity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates only with c076 and c078; the same ambiguity about 'the company' recurs against the policy's defined use of that word for the insurer throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An exception that swallows the rule: excepting personal injury, bodily injury, property damage and hospital professional liability leaves the D&O exclusion with almost nothing to bite on.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also assumes the policy affords 'hospital professional liability' cover, which the Professional Services Excluded endorsement (c082) removes, producing an internal inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence removing all discrimination injury from personal injury; blunt but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It squarely contradicts limb (5) of the personal injury definition (c035), which affirmatively includes racial or religious discrimination not committed by the insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The reproduced text is missing its opening words and connectors, so the exclusion's subject and its 'at any time' qualifier cannot be read coherently from the page.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates in part the Total Pollution Exclusion (c094) and has no counterpart granting asbestos cover elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Again fragmentary; the no-defense sentence has lost the words identifying what relief is sought.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes a defense obligation that Insuring Agreement II(a) (c004) confers, an express carve-out rather than a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'arising out of the rendering of or failure to render ... professional health care services' is broad and its boundary against ordinary hospital negligence (staffing, credentialing, administration) is the classic professional-services line-drawing problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A blanket professional services exclusion cannot easily be reconciled with the Aggregate Limits Endorsement's 'professional liability hazard' (c084), the cross-suits professional carve-out (c060), the contingent excess endorsement (c100-c104) and the professional liability limits endorsement (c121).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line double negative — the exclusion does not apply to entities 'not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' — whose application to any given insured or claim is far from self-evident.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It has to be read with the contingent excess endorsement (c100-c104), which uses a different Fund-based test and disapplies 'Form 035 (12/87)', a form number that does not match the attached 035 WI (1/94).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amended limit language is careful, but the appended words 'or any professional liability hazard' introduce an undefined term that appears nowhere in the definitions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends paragraph III (c013), presupposes professional liability cover that c082 excludes, and its 'amount stated as the aggregate limit in the declarations' ($9,000,000 in Item 3) is displaced by Endorsement No. 4 (c109, $20,000,000).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A closed list of entities with an express denial of automatic coverage for newly acquired entities; specific, apart from odd entries like 'The Ideal Chub'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Named Insured definition (c020) already sweeps in subsidiaries and controlled organisations, so the list and the definition point in different directions on who is a named insured, and later endorsements (c115, c120) keep amending it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, clear deeming rule for cancellation notice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It aligns with Condition 12's first-named-insured rule (c055) but must be squared with the differing notice periods in c065-c067 and c092.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'effective on the inception date of the policy unless otherwise stated herein' works here because Endorsement No. 1's stated effective date is the inception date.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'only with respect to their interest in the operations of the Named Insured' is a materially vague limitation, and the schedule pairs each additional insured with a loosely stated 'insurable interest' such as 'as their interest may appear'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a second, differently limited class of insureds alongside the insured definitions (c029, c031) and the named insureds list (c085), and those insureds' status under the cross-suits exclusion (c059) is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the stated effective date of Endorsement No. 2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear, entity-specific attachment of the collection agency exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion form itself (c099) speaks generally of 'the Insured', so on its own terms it is broader than this endorsement makes it, a modest inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the stated effective date of Endorsement No. 3.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One short sentence promising sixty days' written notice; simple, but it does not say who gives notice or whether it overrides the printed conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly contradicts Condition 12's thirty days (c055) and the ten-day periods in the Cancellation - Wisconsin endorsement (c065, c066, c067), a plain conflict among operative provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A replacement lead-in identifying the superseded exclusion by description rather than by paragraph letter, which requires the reader to locate it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exclusion it replaces (c028) still appears in the policy jacket, so the two pollution provisions coexist on the page with only this sentence resolving them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'pollutants' as an irritant or contaminant applied to a hospital's operations is the archetypal ambiguity, and the hostile-fire carve-out refers to 'subparagraphs (a) and (d)(ii)' where the garbled numbering is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces c028's sudden-and-accidental regime entirely and speaks of 'bodily injury' where the policy's defined term is 'personal injury', a definitional mismatch with c035.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clean two-limb clean-up cost exclusion; specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on the 'pollutants' definition in c096 and coheres with c094.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant, including ... chemicals and waste' is famously open-ended when applied outside industrial pollution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supplies the operative term for c094-c095 and is not qualified anywhere else in the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the pay plan schedule and Condition 1 (c044).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence about when payments are past due.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports, and does not conflict with, the non-payment cancellation right in c066.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'errors or omissions, malpractice or mistake of a professional nature ... in the conduct of the insured's business activities as a collection agency' is bounded by the collection-agency qualifier.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 2 (c090) limits it to Med-Health Financial Services although the form text refers generally to 'the Insured'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A flat statement that no medical malpractice cover is provided for statutory health care providers; definite on its face but leaves 'medical malpractice liability' undefined against the policy's own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the professional services exclusion (c082-c083), its own contingency carve-back (c102), and the aggregate limits reference to a professional liability hazard (c084) and the professional liability limits endorsement (c121), which together make the professional cover position genuinely incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'subsidiaries of holding companies of the named insured' is an odd formulation that leaves the class of covered entities uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expands a statutory definition beyond the statute and interacts with the Named Insured definition (c020) and the named insureds list (c085) in a way that is not obviously consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A three-condition contingency with a further requirement that the underlying policy be 'identified as being listed for contingency coverage purposes' — nothing in Item 7 carries such an identification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That missing identification in the Schedule of Underlying Insurance, plus the interplay with c082-c083 and c121, makes the contingency's operation hard to reconcile with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge ... which the named insured agrees to pay' leaves both amount and timing unilateral and undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same open-ended premium mechanism in c122 and sits against the fixed premium in Item 5 and Condition 1 (c044) and the fixed pay plan (c097).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disapplies 'Form No. 035(12/87) Professional Services Excluded', but the form actually attached is 035 WI (1/94) — a cross-reference error that could be argued to leave the exclusion untouched.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The mismatch is confirmed by the Schedule of Endorsements and the attached form (c082), so this provision's carve-back may not reach the exclusion that is actually in the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'Policy Territory provisions of the Hospital Professional Liability coverage part attached to the policy' and then merely recites a statute, so what it actually changes is unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no Hospital Professional Liability coverage part in this umbrella, the Territory clause (c014) already applies worldwide, and Endorsement No. 5 (c111) deletes this very form as null and void.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'necessarily incurred ... in determining which insurer(s) shall bear the loss' is vague as to what expenses qualify, and the indemnity is payable only if the loss is ultimately determined to fall on this policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps the Other Insurance condition (c052) and the supplementary payments provisions (c003-c007) on who pays coverage-dispute costs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Titled an exclusion yet it obliges the company to pay one-third of a trebled award, and it defines 'damages' to exclude plaintiff's legal fees only 'for purposes of this exclusion' — the two halves pull against each other.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 (c111) deletes Form 009-133 and declares it null and void, yet the form remains in the policy and on the Schedule of Endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 'effective on the inception date' default matches the stated 03/01/1996 effective date of Endorsement No. 4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'the policy limits in Item 2' when limits are stated in Item 3 (Item 2 is the policy period), and the consideration line leaves the additional premium blank — two mechanical defects in one short clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It also raises the declared $18,000,000 occurrence/$9,000,000 aggregate limits to $20,000,000/$20,000,000, so it conflicts with the Declarations and with the limit provisions (c013, c084) as printed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Endorsement No. 5's stated effective date, though that endorsement was issued in June 1996 and back-dated to inception.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear deletion language, but it identifies one form by number alone ('009-133') and the other with a date, and the deletion is back-dated to inception by c110.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both deleted forms (c107 trebled damages, c105 policy territory) remain physically in the policy and on the Schedule of Endorsements, so the instrument as assembled contradicts itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence attaching a replacement form; unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substitutes c113 for c105, but the replaced form is still bound into the policy, leaving two versions of 009-118 in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Like its predecessor, it purports to amend territory provisions of a coverage part that is not part of this policy and otherwise merely quotes a statute (mis-citing s.146.37 as s.446.37).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no Hospital Professional Liability coverage part here and the Territory clause (c014) already applies everywhere, so the endorsement's operative effect on this instrument is obscure.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The endorsement's stated effective date is 07/08/1996 while the boilerplate defaults to the inception date, a small internal tension resolved by 'unless otherwise stated herein'.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It amends 'Form 0098-052' (a typographical error for 009-052) to add one entity; otherwise definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It builds on the Additional Named Insureds endorsement (c085) and, given the back-dating boilerplate versus the 07/08/1996 effective date, the point at which Children's Specialty Group became an insured is not certain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe on its own.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 7 states an effective date of 01/01/1997 while this boilerplate makes it effective at inception unless otherwise stated, so the two dates must be reconciled to know when CMG - Brown Deer Campus became insured.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain addition of one entity as a Named Insured.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds a Named Insured outside Form 009-052 (unlike c115 and c120), and its effective date is contested between the endorsement header (01/01/1997) and the inception-date boilerplate (c116).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Attachment boilerplate; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 8 is dated 11/03/1997, after the policy period expired on 03/01/1997, yet is made effective at inception — a real timing oddity against Item 2 of the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple renaming, though it changes 'Systems' to 'System' — a one-letter difference from every other page of the policy.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Declarations, the endorsement headers and the additional named insureds list all continue to say 'Children's Health Systems, Inc.', so the identity of the first named insured is stated inconsistently across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain addition of two campuses to the named insureds schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Executed after the policy period ended but back-dated by c118 to inception, and it amends the c085 list that c115 also amends; the layering is untidy but not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It raises 'the professional liability limits, for those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' — a doubly conditional class whose membership is not determinable from the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is headed to Policy No. HPP-1996-4104-00, the underlying CGL policy rather than this umbrella, and it presupposes professional liability cover that the professional services exclusion (c082) removes, so its place in this instrument is genuinely incoherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'the Company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' leaves the trigger ('if the need ... is ever required') and the amount wholly indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the same mechanism in c103 and sits against the fixed premium in Item 5, Condition 1 (c044) and the pay plan endorsement.
